chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions who said:
The man would not break (the Fast) during a Month of Ramazan except in a way of Truth.

key_terms.سَبِيلِ حَقٍّ: In the way of truth / for a valid right or justification

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for validly breaking the fast in Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this concise narration by Ibn Abi Umayr underscores the principle that fasting is the default state in Ramadan, and breaking it requires a specific, valid justification (haqq) rather than mere preference. This aligns with the Shia juristic view that exemptions are strictly defined, reinforcing the sanctity of the fast as the norm. The statement serves as a legal maxim reminding believers that any deviation from fasting must be rooted in recognized religious or physical necessity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions who said,
‘The man would not break (the Fast) during a Month of Ramazan except in a way of Truth’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “
He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘One must not stop fasting in the month of Ramadan except in the way of truth.’”
